final_candidates.decision_summary: AlphaMissense 0.999 with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.043) and zero PLM plausibility converge on maximal disruption of the RING domain zinc-coordinating cysteine, abolishing E3 ligase activity.

AlphaMissense 0.999 is the highest observed; slightly higher evolutionary tolerance (0.166) than C24R/C39R marginally reduces confidence but this RING zinc-coordinating residue remains a strong LOF target.
AlphaMissense 0.998 with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.045) and zero PLM plausibility strongly support disruption of this RING domain zinc-coordinating cysteine.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence is convergent across phenotype and evolutionary dimensions; remaining tools are either not applicable or have insufficient reliability to change the ranking.

history.rationale: C61 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain critical for BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimerization and E3 ligase activity. Substitution to glycine disrupts zinc coordination and is a well-characterized pathogenic mutation.
C61 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; disruption abolishes E3 ligase activity, a key tumor-suppressor function. Awaiting phenotype confirmation.
AlphaMissense 0.9904; same position as C61R but slightly lower score, glycine substitution also disrupts zinc coordination.
AlphaMissense 0.990 with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.036) supports disruption, though slightly lower AlphaMissense than the top C→R candidates.
C64 is another zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain. Substitution to arginine abolishes zinc binding and E3 ligase function, a known pathogenic variant.
C64 is another RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; substitution with arginine disrupts zinc coordination and RING function.
AlphaMissense 0.9965; C64 is the fourth zinc-coordinating cysteine of the RING domain.

AlphaMissense 0.997 remains high, but evolutionary tolerance of 0.215 is the highest among candidates, suggesting R at position 64 is somewhat tolerated in homologs, reducing confidence in maximal disruption.
H41 is a zinc-coordinating histidine in the RING domain. Substitution to arginine disrupts the zinc-binding site and impairs BRCA1-BARD1 interaction.
H41 coordinates zinc in the RING domain; disruption impairs E3 ligase activity and BARD1 interaction.
AlphaMissense 0.9824; H41 is in the RING domain but not a direct zinc ligand, slightly less disruptive than cysteine mutations.
Extremely low evolutionary tolerance (0.015) strongly supports disruption of a conserved residue, but higher PLM score (0.267) and slightly lower AlphaMissense (0.982) keep it below the top tier.
C24 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain. Substitution to arginine disrupts the zinc-binding motif and is associated with loss of function.
C24 is a RING domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; disruption should impair RING fold and E3 ligase function.
Highest AlphaMissense score (0.9994) among all candidates; C24 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain critical for E3 ligase activity.
AlphaMissense 0.999 combined with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.043) and zero PLM plausibility strongly converges on this being a highly disruptive LOF mutation in the RING domain.
M1775 is in the C-terminal BRCT domain, critical for phosphoprotein recognition. Substitution to arginine disrupts the phosphopeptide-binding groove and is a known pathogenic variant.
M1775R is a clinically validated pathogenic mutation in the BRCT domain that disrupts phosphopeptide binding, abolishing DNA damage response signaling.
AlphaMissense 0.893; M1775 is in the BRCT domain, known clinically pathogenic variant.
AlphaMissense 0.893 in BRCT domain is good but lower than RING domain candidates; retained as backup.
Y1703 is in the BRCT domain and involved in phosphopeptide binding. Substitution to cysteine disrupts the binding interface and impairs DNA damage signaling.
Y1703 is in the BRCT domain phosphopeptide-binding groove; substitution may impair DNA damage signaling.
AlphaMissense 0.9672; Y1703 is in the BRCT domain involved in phosphoprotein recognition.
AlphaMissense 0.967 in the BRCT domain remains strong but was not evaluated by evolution_msa this round; retained as a solid alternative.
C39 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain. Substitution to arginine disrupts zinc coordination and E3 ligase activity.
C39 is a RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; disruption impairs RING domain integrity.
AlphaMissense 0.9978; C39 is a RING zinc-coordinating residue, mutation disrupts the structural zinc finger.
AlphaMissense 0.998 with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.045) and zero PLM plausibility provides strong convergent evidence for disruptive LOF in the RING domain.
D67 is in the RING domain near the zinc-binding site. Substitution to tyrosine may disrupt local structure and BARD1 interaction.
D67 is near the RING domain; may affect local structure but less directly disruptive than zinc-coordinating residues.
AlphaMissense 0.217 classified as benign; this mutation is unlikely to abolish BRCA1 function.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense 0.217 classified as benign; this mutation is unlikely to abolish BRCA1 function.

history.rationale: Alternative substitution at M1775 in the BRCT domain to lysine, introducing a charge change that disrupts phosphopeptide binding.
Same position as M1775R but lysine may partially compensate due to similar charge; likely less disruptive than arginine.
AlphaMissense 0.879; same position as M1775R with slightly lower pathogenicity prediction.
AlphaMissense 0.879 is the lowest among active candidates; retained but unlikely to enter top 3.
C61 to arginine is another well-known pathogenic substitution at the RING domain zinc-coordinating site, abolishing E3 ligase activity.
Same critical position as C61G but with a larger charged substitution; expected to be equally or more disruptive to zinc coordination.
AlphaMissense 0.9991; C61 coordinates zinc in the RING domain, disruption abolishes ubiquitin ligase function.
AlphaMissense 0.999 is the highest, but evolutionary tolerance of 0.166 (R seen in ~17% of homologs at position 61) slightly weakens the disruption argument relative to C24R/C39R.
